children: continues to retain subscribers despite weaker U.S. viewing trends, giving Deutsche Bank a reason to stay positive after the streaming company's latest earnings report.

Analyst Bryan Kraft maintained a Buy rating and $93 price target, even as Netflix shares fell 5.3% in Wednesday trading after the company reduced its 2026 advertising revenue forecast to $2.7 billion from about $3 billion. Netflix attributed the reduction to delays in rolling out advertising features and integrating systems with advertisers.

Netflix's third-quarter revenue increased 11.8% year over year to $12.87 billion, while operating income rose 37% to $4.46 billion. The company said cancellations improved from a year earlier in every region, including the United States, despite subscription price increases.

International engagement offered another positive signal. Viewing hours in India climbed 24% during the quarter, with local revenue increasing about 18% after currency adjustments. Kraft believes softer U.S. viewing may reflect a weaker content lineup compared with last year rather than a lasting problem.
Netflix expects 2026 revenue of $51.1 billion, up about 13%, and plans to expand its advertising-supported subscription tier into 15 additional countries in 2027.

title: Netflix Stock Rises as Deutsche Bank Sends Bullish Message to Investors
